Acts of Thomas 108-113: Thomas's mission to India is the founding narrative of the Church of the East's Indian branch. Primary hagiographic source. Upgraded to supports. cert=possible appropriate for tradition-based claim.

Seleucia-Ctesiphon as patriarchal seat of Church of the East attested by Synod of 410 and earlier sources. Only contextualizes evidence (Wikipedia). Approved low — needs synodal/patristic upgrade.

Novatianist presence in Alexandria attested by Socrates HE and correspondence of Dionysius of Alexandria. HE 6.43 is about Rome not Alexandria. Approved low — needs Socrates HE passage.

Pharisees in Judea universally attested by Josephus, Gospels, and rabbinic literature. Mark 11:15-18 contextualizes (temple cleansing, chief priests not Pharisees). Approved low — needs better passage (e.g., Matt 23 or Josephus Ant.).

Valentinus taught in Alexandria before Rome (Irenaeus AH 3.4.3, Epiphanius). AH 1.10.1 contextualizes (rule of faith, not Valentinian geography). Approved low — needs AH 3.4.3 or Clement Strom. reference.

Valentinian presence at Carthage attested by Tertullian's anti-Valentinian writings (Adv. Val.). AH 1.11.1 contextualizes doctrine. Approved low — needs Tertullian Adv. Val. passage.
Valentinian presence at Ephesus plausible (Asia Minor was a Gnostic stronghold). AH 1.11.1 + Wikipedia contextualizes. Approved low — needs specific Ephesus attestation.

Irenaeus wrote AH in Gaul specifically to combat Valentinian influence there. HE 5.1 (Lyons persecution letter) contextualizes. Approved low — the strongest case of all these, but needs AH preface passage.

Rejected: The Diatessaron is Tatian's Gospel harmony. Encratism is attributed to Tatian by Irenaeus (AH 1.28.1), not found in the Diatessaron itself. The Diatessaron's text is a harmonized Gospel narrative.
